statusText: Mapped policy state: EA_ON. Tail is 8 with NQ observed at 29,548.50, up 0.03% on the 29,538.75 settle and still inside the same 29,489.75-29,633.75 Globex band that has framed the last three hours. Price drifted back from 29,586.00 without setting a new extreme, so the session continues to deliver oscillation rather than extension. E-mini S&P 500 futures are unchanged at 7,680.50 in a 0.17% range and VIX at 15.90 is only a marginal session high. Stress rises to 79 because Brent broke $100 for the first time since 24 July after U.S. strikes destroyed five Iranian tankers and Iran fired missiles at a U.S. base in Jordan.
recommendation: Tail remains well below the block threshold, so the mapped policy state is EA_ON for both NQ futures and the NAS100 CFD. The narrow evidence-based danger window covers 13:30-15:00 UTC, the U.S. cash open and first full hour, where an oil-driven inflation impulse meeting the opening auction is the most plausible route to repeated extension after failed retracements. A secondary checkpoint sits at 17:00 UTC, where the 10-year note auction into a 4.81% yield coincides with the Apple keynote, and a third at the 19:00 UTC power hour. Existing-position management, exits and emergency protection remain active throughout. Stress at 79 describes a difficult macro environment, not a mean-reversion failure, and on its own it does not change the mapped state.
headline: NQ holds the 29,489.75-29,633.75 band at 29,548.50 with no new extreme and tail steady at 8, while Brent's break above $100 and missile exchanges over Jordan lift stress to 79
body: At the assessment cutoff the Nasdaq-100 still shows no evidence of mean-reversion failure. NQ futures trade at 29,548.50, up 9.75 points or 0.03% on the 29,538.75 settle, inside a Globex range of 29,489.75-29,633.75 that is unchanged for a third consecutive hour. That is the central observation: the 29,633.75 high has now gone untested through three hourly assessments, and price has instead drifted back from 29,586.00 toward the middle of a band 144 points or 0.49% wide. Investing.com corroborates the level at 29,550.00 against the same 29,538.75 previous close. E-mini S&P 500 futures reinforce the reading, unchanged at 7,680.50 in a 7,678.00-7,691.25 range only 0.17% wide. VIX at 15.90 has set a marginal session high against a 15.72 close but remains absolutely low, and its 15.57-15.90 day range shows no volatility expansion. Cross-asset conditions are conflicted rather than aligned, which historically raises stress more than tail. The macro backdrop deteriorated over the past hour. Brent crude trades at $100.56, up 2.70% on the day, breaching $100 for the first time since 24 July. The driver is a sharp geopolitical escalation: U.S. Central Command destroyed five IRGC-linked oil tankers, four in the Gulf of Oman and one near Kharg Island, Iran's primary crude export terminal, after two Iranian ballistic missile attempts against a U.S. Navy warship. Iran retaliated with ballistic missiles at a U.S. base in Jordan, of which Jordanian air defences intercepted eighteen, and the IRGC issued an explicit warning that tankers at anchor or docked off Kuwait and Bahrain will be targeted. Houthi strikes on Saudi energy infrastructure add a second supply channel. Rates confirm the inflation transmission: the 10-year Treasury yield is 4.807%, up 1.3 basis points and the highest since October 2023, with the 2-year at 4.42%. European equities have taken the drag, with the STOXX 600 down 0.7% at 645.34, the DAX down 0.7% and the CAC 40 down 0.9%, while U.S. futures have stabilised after the prior session closed with the S&P 500 down 0.58% and the Nasdaq Composite down 0.32%. Roughly 60% of a 25 basis point Fed hike is priced for 16 September, which makes Friday's CPI and Thursday's PPI consequential. The tail judgement separates this macro stress from price-path pathology. None of the structural markers are present: there are no shallow-pullback sequences, no repeated extension after failed retracements, no holding near a session extreme, and no abnormal gap or opening structure. The IRGC targeting warning is a genuine unresolved discontinuity mechanism and is the main reason tail is not lower, but a threat that has not yet transmitted into price is not observed evidence of a no-retracement path. Semiconductor strength, which offset oil pressure in the prior session with SMH up 1.2%, is a further reason a one-way index path is not the base case. Delayed cross-asset context collected earlier in the session was more than 90 minutes old at the cutoff and was therefore treated as stale supporting colour only, with all price-path conclusions drawn from current primary sources.

lookbackSummary: Across the preceding 24 clock-hours the mapped state stayed EA_ON throughout, with tail between 5 and 15 and no reading approaching the block threshold. The single elevated print was 15 at 14:00 UTC on 8 September during a brief trend-down phase in the first full U.S. cash hour, and it reverted within the same hour. One hour, 09:00 UTC on 8 September, has no published assessment and is marked unavailable. Stress climbed steadily from 68 to 77 over the period as crude advanced through $99 and then above $100 on Middle East supply disruption, the 10-year held near cycle highs and Fed hike pricing firmed toward 60%. The pattern of the whole period is consistent: rising macro stress with repeatedly orderly, two-sided price discovery in the index.
outlookSummary: The next 24 hours contain no Tier-1 U.S. macro release; PPI and jobless claims on 10 September and CPI on 11 September, both at 12:30 UTC, fall outside the window. Conditional tail stays in a 6-12 band and never approaches the block threshold, peaking at 12 across the 13:30-15:00 UTC U.S. cash open, where an oil-driven inflation impulse meeting the opening auction is the specific failure mode of concern. Secondary steps sit at 17:00 UTC, where the 10-year note auction into a 4.81% yield coincides with the Apple keynote and is labelled event/whipsaw for two-sided reaction risk, and at the 19:00 UTC power hour. Conditional tail then eases to a 6-7 trough across the Asian handover before returning to 8 through the European session. Forecast confidence decays from 88 to 76 with evidence age, not because risk is judged to rise. The main unresolved discontinuity route is a Middle East headline arriving into a thin overnight book, given the IRGC warning to tankers off Kuwait and Bahrain.
